Can't maintain interest in games for too long ? Must be depression.

This one is actually plausible. The first time I read someone give depression or loneliness as a cause for not enjoying games, it really struck me as true for myself. It's not just games, it could be anything probably. Lack of social interaction can be suffocating in a way to where I was not enjoying anything in my life. As a games enthusiast, video games were the most noticeable aspect that should have be providing joy to me based on lifelong interest. Obviously this is not always the case, but can really be an eye opening response for people who haven't put two and two together.

As someone who's bipolar, this is actually kind of legitimate. Part of depression can be a lack of interest in the things you're normally interested in. There's very few things that hold me through when I'm having a bout. My shows is one of them, probably because I only have them once a week. Flash, Arrow, Shield. I've been gaming a lot less lately. My wife will leave for a bit, and I'll be thinking "yes! time to game!" and end up only spending half an hour gaming(out of say 2ish hours). Sometimes this is because I'll find myself switching games. Start a game up, get into the menu, looking through settings, and get bored before I start. I wouldn't take it as a sure-fire sign of depression though. If I didn't have a diagnosis, there'd have to be more warning signs for me to start thinking it's the case.
It's important to note that he was only mentioning a possibility in this case. I don't see anything wrong with users sharing their relevant experiences.

I've been milling around ideas of how to implement this sub. I've seen of lot intelligent discussion on the site, which is very encouraging. I would really like to see a formal debate format, something I haven't yet seen on a site like this. I'm also a huge fan of the Intelligence Squared debates, which implement Oxford-Style debating. Of course, I would like input from the voat community, so I don't want to go into too much detail with too many of the specific ideas I've had yet.

Currently, the sub is closed to new submissions. I've had the notion that mods would submit the debate motion (which is somehow decided by the community) and add the debaters to the list of approved submitters during the debate rounds. When the debate is concluded, those submitters are removed from the list and the cycle repeats. This would prevent off topic submissions and non-participants from disrupting, as well as allowing the debaters to be chosen from within the community.

I've had some other ideas, but I'll leave this here hoping enough people in /v/all/new see it and weigh in.

I much preferred unstructured debates where they are basically shouting matches but that would be difficult to do in this setting. Having two people debate a topic for a set amount of time would be the kind of debate I would like to see the only rules would be ones such as no personal attacks and rules like that. I would very much like to see this sub thrive and would love to be involved in debates.
